resources.string: How muscles turn the shoulder blade
Scapular upward rotation

A simplified back view of the right shoulder during normal arm elevation. Colored arrows indicate approximate directions of muscle pull, not force values. Blue marks show position or motion. Other three-dimensional motions are not shown.
Three regions and a partner

The upper trapezius reaches the outer clavicle, the middle region reaches the acromion and scapular spine, and the lower region reaches the inner end of that spine. The serratus anterior wraps from the ribs to the front side of the inner edge of the scapula.
Support at the shoulder girdle

The upper trapezius helps elevate the outer clavicle. The middle region pulls inward and helps steady the scapula as the other muscles turn it. These actions overlap rather than switching on in order.
Pulls work together

The lower trapezius pulls the inner end of the scapular spine down and inward. The serratus anterior draws the lower part of the blade around the ribs. Together these pulls help turn the blade upward, with support from the upper trapezius through the clavicle.
The socket turns upward
As the blade rotates, its lower tip swings outward around the rib cage and its socket turns upward with the rising arm. The pale outline shows the starting position of the blade.
The blade follows the arm down
As the arm lowers, the blade turns back toward its starting position. The muscles continue to coordinate; the drawing does not assign fixed amounts of motion or muscle load.
